scope: Proposition 2.2 (Prime-product displacement inequality) of the manuscript “Edit Distance in l1: Matching Bounds up to Constants in the Exponent” (preprints/Edit-Distance-in-l1-Matching-Bounds-up-to-Constants-in-the-Exponent-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 099 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c554cfee6ede3e18), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 4. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let b, h ≥ 1 be integers, let P ≥ 1, and let G1, . . . , Gb be finite abelian groups. Suppose vj ∈ Gj has order pj, where p1, . . . , pb are distinct primes in [P, 2P]. In G = Qb j=1 Gj, use the same notation vj for the element acting only in coordinate j, and put τ = Pb j=1 vj. Then every H : G → ℓ1 and every integer u satisfy VH(uv1) ≤ (2P)2h VH(τ) + 2 h b X j=1 Ea∈Z/pjZVH(avj). (2.3)
